{01}

Synthetic exposure.

A perpetual position tracks price exposure. It is not a share, does not provide dividends, and does not confer ownership or shareholder rights.

{02}

Leverage and gaps.

Leveraged positions can lose all posted collateral. Thin stocks can gap sharply, trade with limited depth, or enter exchange halts. A liquidation estimate does not guarantee an exit price.

{03}

Oracle and software risk.

Multiple sources and attestation do not make an oracle infallible. Data may be stale, dispersed, or unavailable. Enclave, smart-contract, keeper, or other software failures can affect execution and settlement.

{04}

Liquidity and insurance.

Vault liquidity can be constrained. Insurance and staked tranches can be exhausted. The specified loss waterfall may expose LP principal in a declared default.

{05}

Market availability.

Confidence-band limits, halts, corporate actions, delistings, and jurisdiction restrictions can suspend or limit access. Planned 24/7 operation is conditional on valid prices and applicable risk rules.

{06}

This site is simulated.

The current dashboard uses fictional markets and virtual funds. No financial transaction occurs, and the preview should not be treated as investment advice or a representation of a live service.
